claims.claim: Nikon z fc is a retro-inspired, slr-style mirrorless camera featuring a 20.9-megapixel aps-c...
claims.evidence: The photos show a Nikon Z fc body (photo 0 and photo 1). The megapixel/spec text itself is not verifiable from the photos.
Photos show “Nikon” and “Z fc” on the camera body (photo 0 and photo 1), not Canon.

risks.risk: Seller text conflicts with photos (Canon claimed, Nikon shown). This can indicate wrong listing, bait-and-switch, or poor credibility.
risks.proof: Ask the seller to confirm the exact model name and brand on camera (send a photo of the top plate showing “Nikon Z fc” and the serial number area).
risks.if_unproven: Price as Nikon Z fc but treat as potentially mismatched/uncertain bundle; keep at the lower end of comparable mirrorless pricing.

risks.risk: Lens model is not fully readable; the included lens could be different from what you expect (affects value).
risks.proof: Request a clear close-up photo of the lens front ring and the full lens label (model name/number) and mount confirmation.
risks.if_unproven: Price as body + unknown/entry lens (worst case: less valuable lens), not as a premium kit.

risks.risk: Condition/working status (sensor, shutter count, autofocus, IBIS, buttons) cannot be confirmed from photos.
risks.proof: Request a short video showing: power on, menu navigation, autofocus on a face/object, and a sample photo at 1x and 10x zoom (or a focus test).
risks.if_unproven: Price as not fully proven—assume typical used wear and no guarantee of perfect function.

risks.risk: Battery health and charger compatibility are unknown.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo of battery label (model/capacity) and a clip showing charging indicator / battery percentage after charging.
risks.if_unproven: Price as standard used battery (not new), and assume charger may be generic/uncertain unless proven.

proof_requests: Send a clear photo of the camera top plate showing “Nikon Z fc” plus the serial number area (for authenticity).
Send a clear close-up of the lens model text (front ring and side label) to confirm exactly which lens is included.
Send a short working test video: power on + menu, autofocus lock on, and one sample photo (daylight) showing sharpness.
Send battery label photo and a clip showing it charging/holding power (battery percentage after use).
response.reason: The photos clearly show a Nikon Z fc, but the seller’s text claims Canon (credibility issue). Also, the exact lens model and working condition are not provable from the provided images, so a confident price pick from comparables isn’t safe yet.
